title: Global carbon emissions set to fall in 2026 due to Iran energy shock | New Scientist
description: Carbon dioxide emissions are projected to fall 0.4 per cent this year, driven in part by higher oil prices resulting from disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz
author: Shosha Adie

title: Cold therapy may be worse than doing nothing for post-exercise recovery | New Scientist
description: Many are convinced that ice baths or cold showers are an effective way to speed recovery after exercise, but a study finds that cold therapy may actually have the opposite effect
author: Tosin Thompson

title: X chromosome gene may reduce autism rates in women and girls | New Scientist
description: A gene called ZFX exerts powerful effects on an entire network of genes linked to autism, which may help explain why the condition is less common in females
author: Michael Marshall

title: Prehistoric Britons may have made giant stone axes to show off | New Scientist
description: Unusually large handaxes weighing up to 3 kilograms have puzzled archaeologists because they are so unwieldy, but their function may have been purely symbolic
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre

title: Weird 'ultraquantum' turbulence seen for the first time | New Scientist
description: An experiment with ultracold potassium atoms has revealed details of a type of turbulence that only exists in the quantum realm and relies on odd tangles of stringy whirlpools
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Antipersonnel mines have returned in Ukraine and now threaten the world | New Scientist
description: 3D printing, microcontrollers and drones have enabled the resurgence of antipersonnel mines in the Russia-Ukraine war, making mines deadlier and more accessible
author: David Hambling
